quotes.text: We curated a subset of 26 patient cases from the HANCOCK dataset

rationale: The paper names source datasets and relates benchmark cases and questions to those sources. It does not report a complete version or snapshot date plus platform and a full task-to-source-record route.
The packet states data origin and licensing for the benchmark sources. It does not document consent, IRB status, or an explicit statement that such review was not required.

quotes.text: For each selected patient, an average of 40 modality-specific files are available

rationale: The paper provides descriptive statistics and sampling details for the selected cases. It does not compare the sample against a named target population.
searched: S1 paper and appendix, S2 README/docs, S3 release notes, S4 code, S5 agent-visible prompts. The packet does not report dedicated unsafe-output or bias tests.
searched: S1 paper and appendix, S2 README/docs, S3 release notes, S4 code, S5 agent-visible prompts. No developer-side contamination control or measured contamination check is reported.
searched: S1 paper and appendix, S2 README/docs, S3 release notes, S4 code, S5 agent-visible prompts. The benchmark does not report that agents are isolated from ground-truth results at run time.

searched: S1 paper and appendix, S2 README/docs, S3 release notes, S4 code, S5 agent-visible prompts. The packet does not pin data, software, harness, and live external dependencies sufficiently for a frozen release.

quotes.text: the final set of questions in MTBBench were sent for external manual review by domain specialists

rationale: The benchmark reports clinician review of question-answer pairs, which is manual solvability and correctness evidence. It does not report a scripted reference solution run through the grader.

searched: S1 paper and appendix, S2 README/docs, S3 release notes, S4 code, S5 agent-visible prompts. The benchmark tasks are question-answering and file/tool access tasks; the packet does not describe tasks that change environment state.

quotes.text: outcome and recurrence prediction remain the most difficult, with accuracies near random (50%)

rationale: The paper discloses a chance-like rate for some tasks and uses multiple-choice or true/false formats. This is a disclosed weakness rather than an empirical trivial-agent result.
searched: S1 paper and appendix, S2 README/docs, S3 release notes, S4 code, S5 agent-visible prompts. No do-nothing or random-agent score is reported.

searched: S1 paper and appendix, S2 README/docs, S3 release notes, S4 code, S5 agent-visible prompts. The packet reports objective answer parsing, but not validation of the automatic evaluator on benchmark outputs.
A decoding safeguard is visible in code for the OpenAI evaluator. The paper/docs do not state seeds or a repeated-run policy for the full harness.

quotes.text: Mean accuracy and 95% confidence intervals of various LLMs by task

rationale: The paper reports mean accuracy with 95% confidence intervals for model comparisons across tasks. It also describes bootstrap resampling for those intervals.

searched: S1 paper and appendix, S2 README/docs, S3 release notes, S4 code, S5 agent-visible prompts. S1-S3 do not report the number of independent runs per task, a seed or sampling policy for model runs, or run independence.

quotes.text: we sample with replacement from the set of question outcomes per model

rationale: The paper reports CIs and states the bootstrap resampling unit as question outcomes or patient-question pairs. It does not address clustering of tasks within patients.
searched: S1 paper and appendix, S2 README/docs, S3 release notes, S4 code, S5 agent-visible prompts. No action-level, state-level, pass^k, or identical-rerun reliability metric is reported.

quotes.text: we use the gpt-4o-2024-08-06 checkpoint for gpt4o

rationale: The paper gives exact snapshot identifiers for the OpenAI models and names other evaluated model families. It does not report decoding parameters or a harness commit/tag matching the reported numbers.

quotes.text: To use CONCH you must provide the H&E image name and extension and a list of options

rationale: The benchmark defines text-command formats for requesting files and using tools, and the prompts describe file reads/tool use to the agent. Return semantics including errors or failure returns are not documented on reporting surfaces.

searched: S1 paper and appendix, S2 README/docs, S3 release notes, S4 code, S5 agent-visible prompts. The packet does not report tool conformance tests or a disclosure of simulated, stubbed, or no-op tool behavior reaching the agent.

searched: S1 paper and appendix, S2 README/docs, S3 release notes, S4 code, S5 agent-visible prompts. The packet describes file requests, tool queries, and final answers, not clinical orders, prescriptions, notes, messages, or other write actions.

quotes.text: Model outputs are parsed using regular expressions to extract answers.

rationale: The paper states that the grader reads the model answer string and justifies this by using objective multiple-choice/true-false accuracy. It does not validate the grader on labelled correct and incorrect outcomes with per-class error rates.

searched: S1 paper and appendix, S2 README/docs, S3 release notes, S4 code, S5 agent-visible prompts. No controls on answer leakage through tools/retrieval, held-out/private split, or canary/provenance marker are reported.

quotes.text: Mean accuracy and 95% confidence intervals of various LLMs by task

rationale: The paper reports results by benchmark task family and gives dataset/task sizes elsewhere. It does not report results per patient demographic subgroup despite demographic fields being present.

quotes.text: a clinicogenomic resource of cancer patients linking genomic profiles with structured clinical timelines

rationale: The paper states the source of patient records and separate data licences/terms for source datasets. It does not report IRB, DUA, credentialing, or de-identification method.
